newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods leap, gasoline reasserts itself.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods leap, gasoline reasserts itself.

text.p: U.S. spot products reversed direction and scored sharp gains by late Friday, players said, with gasoline humbling its detractors by soaring on NYMEX futures and stable differentials.

New York Harbor A4-grade reformulated gasoline rocketed 1.60 cents higher, with diffs little changed at about 0.20-cent below the print, traders said. And NYH conventional unleaded M4 jumped 1.80 cents amid slighter firmer diffs.
Traders said gasoline, which has been throttled in recent weeks as heating oil hogged the spotlight, was benefitting as refiners cut back production in order to maximize distillates ahead of winter.

Much of the focus remained on jet fuel, as differentials on New York 54-grade firmed about a half cent, clawing back only a fraction of Thursday's two-cent slide spurred by heavy selling of Colonial Pipeline product, players said.
"It can't come off too much lower because it's barely above heating oil differentials," one East Coast jet trader said, noting bids stood at about 0.25 cent over the print.
Diffs on NYH 55-grade low-sulfur jet eased 0.75-cent to 4.75 cents above October futures -- tightening Thursday's 5.50 cent spread between low and high-sulfur grades.
